description: Verify that TCP uses clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers (RFC 1122 §4.2.2.9 p87, RFC 793 §3.3 p27)
approach:
[Objective]
Two back-to-back active OPENs must produce different ISNs — RFC 793 calls for a clock-driven generator. A static or counter-based ISN would let attackers predict / inject sequence numbers.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Cycle 1: DUT active OPEN → DUT → Tester: SYN with ISN_1 → snapshot ISN_1.
2. Tester → DUT: ABORT to release the binding.
3. Cycle 2: DUT active OPEN → DUT → Tester: SYN with ISN_2.

[Pass condition]
ISN_1 ≠ ISN_2 (and ideally separated by clock-driven jitter).

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_cycle1_isn / Fail_no_cycle2_isn — SYN capture missed
• Fail_isn_unchanged — DUT reused a prior ISN across active OPENs

verdicts.Pass: DUT chose distinct ISNs across active OPENs — normal
verdicts.Fail_isn_unchanged: DUT reused prior ISN across active OPENs
